A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NAtS-L research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original language-model evaluations, retrieval and context-extrapolation results, latency measurements and ablations.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by sparse-attention comparisons, additional ablations, temporal analyses and a Mamba2-based variant.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces and evaluates a NAtS-L variant combining softmax attention with Mamba2 instead of GDN. The original GDN-based architecture remains; expanded descriptions of its decoding and weight normalization do not establish a redesign.

E1.justification: Fineweb-Edu training and the original language-modeling, commonsense, retrieval, RULER and LongBench coverage remain. New comparisons and analyses reuse existing tasks and corpora, including PG19, NarrativeQA and CodeParrot.

E2.justification: New Appendix B/Table 5 evaluates NSA, MOBA, GDN with sliding-window attention, FlexPrefill, SnapKV, AdaKV and PyramidKV. Figure 7 adds FlexPrefill and SnapKV to latency comparisons. These substantially expand the evaluated alternatives beyond v1's original comparator set.

E3.justification: The new sparse-method comparison specifies 380M models, a 50% computational budget for sparse variants and a 1024-token GDN sliding window. Table 4 adds a 128-token chunk experiment. Original training budgets, context lengths and benchmark protocols remain; the default 64-token chunk size is newly disclosed.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds sigmoid versus linear output-weight activation and larger-chunk ablations. Section 5.2 and Appendix C.5 add temporal routing and output-weight analyses across three corpora, extending v1's aggregate token-distribution analysis substantially.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-level uncertainty estimates. The additional results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original table rows and plotted results are unchanged. New results include retrieval averages of 30.02, 30.57 and 27.85 for the added ablations versus 33.49 for the default, and 25.34 versus 19.25 for NAtS-L Mamba2 versus Mamba2. Table 5 adds sparse-baseline results, but its NAtS-L Hybrid NQ score of 20.72 differs unexplainedly from 16.53 in retained Table 6.

T1.justification: Equation 22 explicitly defines softmax-normalized mixing weights, whereas v1 specified the weighted output combination and described weights only through linear projections. The new routing argmax restates existing highest-score selection; the original gradient and state-update derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: adaptive token-level mixing of linear and softmax attention improves long-context modeling while reducing computational latency.

C2.justification: v2 interprets temporal routing and weight distributions as supporting context-dependent allocation and time-dependent mixing. It also interprets the Mamba2 experiment as evidence of architectural generality and explains the flexibility cost of larger chunks. Existing limitations and future directions remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the default 64-token chunk size, softmax normalization of head-wise output weights, and cache/state updates and rollback during token generation. Hardware, optimizer settings, training budgets and the code-access location are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix B substantially expand positioning through five families of sparse and hybrid attention, distinguishing fixed budgets, learned selection and approximation of full attention. Added works include FlexPrefill, AdaKV, PyramidKV, SeerAttention and AttentionPredictor. Publication updates to existing references do not constitute additional works.

P1.justification: v2 adds focused methodological explanations and analysis paragraphs, introduces Appendix B and subsection C.2, and updates conference front matter and bibliography metadata. Most original prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds temporal-distribution Figures 6, 11 and 12, sparse-comparison latency Figure 7, and Tables 5 and 9, while expanding Table 4. Existing displays are retained and relocated, table captions move above tables, and Figure 1's legend changes from Inter-Chunk to Intra-Chunk.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central accuracy-efficiency argument by adding evaluations against relevant sparse-attention and KV-compression competitors missing from v1. Targeted ablations, the Mamba2 variant and decoding details also improve the evidence and assessability of the framework. Unexplained NQ discrepancies between Tables 5 and 6 weaken numerical consistency, but the broader comparative and diagnostic gains remain substantial.
